precepts.text: All things are double, one against another, and he hath made nothing imperfect. Satan was created to do exactly what he does, and one thing establisheth the good of another. When Satan attacks and we are not devoured, we become better.
precepts.point: Even the worst things, like Job losing his kids, are to make us perfect. It is a hard saying, but without Satan our adversary we cannot become perfect.
precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another”. God created good, and he created evil also. He “hath made nothing imperfect”: Satan was not created imperfect. He was created to do exactly what he is doing, walking about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

“One thing establisheth the good or another”. What establishes the good of us and makes us perfect? When we go through temptation, when Satan attacks us and we overcome and are not devoured by him. Satan does devour some; some brothers and sisters get devoured. But those that are not devoured become better and become perfect. That is why Peter says “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect”. It is a hard saying, but without Satan, our adversary, we cannot become perfect, because it is his job and his children's job to try us, and as they try us they make us better. Even the real bad things: Job lost all his kids, and that was to make him perfect.

So learn how to fight him and how to see him when he is attacking. See him when he is coming, when he is trying to jump on you and put thoughts in your mind, and say, get out of my mind, Satan. Don't wait until he puts the thought there and you act on it, and afterward you are like Judas, what did I do? That is why the scripture says be vigilant: vigilant means you are watching.

And “who shall be filled with beholding his glory?” Those of us made perfect in trials and tribulation are the ones who will behold the Lord's glory.

precepts.text: All things are double one against another, and he hath made nothing imperfect.
precepts.point: Satan and evil were created too, and everything is made in pairs.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another: and he hath made nothing imperfect.” Everything is made in pairs. When God divided the light from the darkness he made good and evil as a pair, and Satan and evil were created too. Nothing got into creation by mistake. There is always a counter, good set against evil all the time: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

Look at what Genesis 1 mentions first, before the earth was formed: the waters of the deep, which is space, covered in darkness. Darkness is mentioned before the light because the Lord had it set from the beginning that, when we came down here, we would be evil anyway.

That is why “the evening and the morning were the first day”: the evening comes before the morning. That is why Cain was born first, Ishmael came before Isaac, and Esau, Edom, was born before Jacob. The evil, the darkness, goes first, and then the light comes after, which is why Christ said the first shall be last and the last shall be first. The double of Sirach, darkness set against light, runs through all of Genesis.

precepts.text: The father waketh for the daughter when no man knoweth; keep a sure watch, lest she be defiled and made a reproach.
precepts.point: The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters. Have a care of their body; do not give overmuch liberty; the father wakes for the daughter and the care for her takes away sleep. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

precepts.why:
“The father waketh for the daughter, when no man knoweth; and the care for her taketh away sleep”: when she is young, “In her virginity, lest she should be defiled and gotten with child in her father’s house”, and when she is married, lest she misbehave or be barren. “Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people”.

That is the charge Dinah's story presses. She went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem the son of Hamor “took her, and lay with her, and defiled her”: stranger rape, and a reproach on the house of Jacob. The father wakes for the daughter, and the care for her takes away sleep: keep a sure watch, so that she is not defiled. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

precepts.text: Be not ashamed of much correction of children, nor to make the side of an evil servant to bleed.
precepts.point: The wisdom writings teach not to be ashamed of much correction of children, nor of making the side of an evil servant to bleed. An evil servant that will not get right could be corrected physically, so long as he was not killed.

note.label: Exodus 21: The Judgments Set Before Israel

precepts.why:
If a man smite his servant with a rod and he die under his hand, “he shall be surely punished”; but if he continue a day or two, “he shall not be punished: for he is his money.” The wisdom writings teach the same: “Of these things be not thou ashamed, and accept no person to sin thereby”, and among them, “of much correction of children; and to make the side of an evil servant to bleed.”

Do not be ashamed of much correction of children, nor of making the side of an evil servant to bleed. An evil servant that will not get right could be corrected physically, so long as he was not killed.

precepts.text: The father waketh for the daughter when no man knoweth; keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter.
precepts.point: When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

note.label: Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy

precepts.why:
“The father waketh for the daughter, when no man knoweth; and the care for her taketh away sleep: when she is young, lest she pass away the flower of her age.” The flower of her age is her virginity being taken. The father’s charge is to watch over her: know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures.

“Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people.” Keeping that watch is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness.

precepts.point: This is why records must be kept, especially where money is concerned; all things touching the body must be put in writing.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

precepts.why:
“Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing that thou givest out, or receivest in.”

That is how the money for the house was handled. Jehoiada set a chest with a hole bored in the lid beside the altar, and when there was much money the king’s scribe and the high priest came up, “and told the money that was found in the house of the Lord”, and gave it into the hands of them that did the work.

This is why records must be kept, especially where money is concerned. All things touching the body must be put in writing.

precepts.text: We are supposed to put all things in writing, for evidence is the only way to prove something.
precepts.point: Anathoth was in the country of Benjamin because the priests were given cities and suburbs to dwell in.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
Jeremiah did not just hand over the money for the field. He weighed him seventeen shekels of silver in the balances, subscribed the evidence, sealed it, took witnesses, and kept both the sealed evidence and the open according to the law and custom, then delivered it to Baruch the son of Neriah before all the Jews in the court of the prison.

That is the law: “Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing that thou givest out, or receivest in.” We are supposed to put all things in writing. Evidence is the only way to prove something, and Jeremiah's purchase of the field in Anathoth, in the country of Benjamin where the priests were given cities and suburbs to dwell in, was done in number and weight and in writing.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“I will now remember the works of the Lord, and declare the things that I have seen: In the words of the Lord are his works.”

The works of the Lord are his words: his law, statutes and commandments. That is why the works of the law that justify no flesh cannot be the commandments themselves, whose doers are justified; they are the works of the sacrificial law of Moses that could not take away sins.

Being defiled by women is an allegory, a similitude, in terms of philosophies; the first philosophy came through Eve, and we all die. “And sit not in the midst of women.” “For from garments cometh a moth, and from women wickedness”: the Most High knows what he made.

“Behold not every body’s beauty, and sit not in the midst of women.” Two types of men hang around groups of women: hungry brothers, because they are trying to get the cookies, and homos, who want your beauty secrets, how you do your makeup, your hair, your nails. Too much hand gesture; if your hands are on your hip you better be tired. “For from garments cometh a moth, and from women wickedness.”

It was a shame, and we have to bring that shame back: “In her virginity, lest she should be defiled and gotten with child in her father’s house.” Today it is socially acceptable, with new titles like baby daddy.
